name: American Psycho morning routine edits

lead: American Psycho morning routine edits are short videos that take the grooming and fitness scenes of the 2000 film American Psycho and present them as aspirational self-care. The appearance payoff is a polished, consistent routine of skincare, hair and exercise.

The film's character Patrick Bateman is obsessed with his appearance, and a facial-mask scene is among its best-known moments. Some viewers read Bateman as a 'sigma male' or hustle-culture emblem, though many read the film as a critique of capitalism.

paras: Creators cut the film's routine footage to music and overlay it with their own, covering ordinary skincare steps, hair, gym time and tidy dressing. Followers use the edit as a prompt to build a consistent morning routine.

The risks are social rather than physical: the character is a fictional serial killer, and some commentators say admiring him misreads the satire. The skincare and exercise elements themselves are ordinary.

angle.text: The edits give people a vivid template for a disciplined routine: skincare, grooming and exercise done every morning. Followers treat it as motivation for keeping up their appearance.

lead: American Psycho morning routine edits are fan-made videos that repackage the grooming scenes of the 2000 film American Psycho, directed by Mary Harron from Bret Easton Ellis's 1991 novel, as a self-care template [1]. The film premiered at Sundance on January 21, 2000 and opened in the US on April 14, 2000 [1].
Patrick Bateman, played by Christian Bale, is obsessed with his appearance; the facial-mask scene was reportedly filmed in one take [1]. Bale trained at the gym for hours for the role [1].

The film has a cult following that grew from the mid-2000s and became visible on social media in the 2010s; Bateman is a frequent meme subject, and some viewers admire him as a 'sigma male' and an emblem of hustle culture while many read the film as criticising capitalism [1]. Looksmaxxing-adjacent forums have also joked about 'Patrick Bateman abs' and shared the character's morning routine video [2].
infobox: Patrick Bateman, played by Christian Bale [1]

paras: The film grossed about $34.2 million on a $7 million budget and drew mostly positive reviews [1]. Its cult following and meme presence built over the 2000s and 2010s [1]. Bateman has been referenced in music videos and parodies [1].
Admirers treat Bateman as an image of discipline and grooming; others stress that the film is a satire of capitalism and that the character is a murderer [1].
A T Nation forum poster once joked about 'Patrick Bateman abs' and linked a video of the character's morning routine [2].

timeline.event: Bret Easton Ellis publishes the novel American Psycho [1].
